name: PAD Major Amputation Non-Home Discharge Validation
remarks: PAD / MAJOR LE AMPUTATION — NON-HOME DISCHARGE VALIDATION MODULE
External validation of two integer risk scores for non-home discharge
(NHD) after major lower extremity amputation:
1. Iannuzzi 2020 (J Vasc Surg 71:889) — 9 components, 0–18 pts
2. Subramaniam 2018 mFI-5 (J Am Coll Surg 226:173) — 5 components, 0–5 pts
STUDY DESIGN
Target  : inpatient major LE amputation (AKA / BKA / through-knee /
hip disarticulation / hemipelvectomy / ankle disart), age >= 18,
with at least ONE of PAD, diabetes mellitus, or LE wound
documented on or before the index date.
Outcome : non-home discharge (to SNF or IRF) — captured at the index
inpatient encounter's discharge_disposition (NUBC code), mapped
to visit_occurrence.discharged_to_concept_id by the ETL.
Design  : prognostic model external validation, integer risk score.
See     : study_params.yaml, cohorts/target_amputation.sql,
cohorts/outcome_nhd.sql, covariates/covariates.csv,
covariates/covariates_mfi5.csv
CLINICAL PATHWAY
Phase 1  Age guard (min 60) + onset delay (0–25 yr) + age cap (95)
Phase 2  Indication assignment — 5 paths cover PAD-only, PAD+DM,
DM-only, PAD+Wound, Wound-only. Every patient receives at
least one qualifying indication condition.
Phase 3  Indication outpatient encounter (open through all covariate states)
Phase 4  Covariate cascade — generates conditions / observations /
drug exposures covering both Iannuzzi and mFI-5 score components.
Tissue loss (Iannuzzi) and diabetes mellitus (mFI-5) are
intentionally OMITTED from the cascade — they are issued by
the indication paths in Phase 2 and double-coding them here
would inflate prevalence and add duplicate condition_occurrence
rows. Effective prevalences from the indication mix:
tissue_loss  ~25% (PAD+Wound 15% + Wound-only 10%, ulcer only)
dm           ~40% (PAD+DM 25% + DM-only 15%)
Iannuzzi-specific:
ambu_deficit [3 pts]  20% (walking aid use observation)
insulin_dep  [2 pts]  16% (insulin glargine medication)
anemia       [2 pts]  11% (Hgb < 10 g/dL; Hgb measured for ALL)
mFI-5-specific:
copd          [1 pt mFI-5]  15%
chf           [1 pt mFI-5]  20%
htn           [1 pt mFI-5]  65% (very common in elderly amputation pop)
fs_dep        [1 pt mFI-5]  25% (frailty 60% / impaired mobility 40%)
Demographic components (age decades, female, nonwhite) are read
directly from person.year_of_birth / gender_concept_id / race_concept_id
and require no module states.
NOTE: The ischemic gangrene ancestor (4291464) is NOT exercised
in synthetic data — only ischemic ulcer (4029926) is generated
via the indication paths. To exercise the gangrene branch, split
the wound-bearing indication paths to issue 13954005 (70%) or
402861007 (30%) as in the OLER reference module.
Phase 5  Treatment strategy oversampling: 10% non-exposed / 90% exposed.
Close the outpatient encounter via path-end EncounterEnd states.
Phase 6  Pre-amputation workup delay (7–90 days — shorter than OLER pathway
because major amputation is often urgent for advanced CLI/wound).
Phase 7  Inpatient amputation admission. All exposed patients pass through
PT (50%) and palliative care (10%) consult checks. Geriatric
consult (30%) is gated to patients > 75 only.
AKA (40%) or BKA (60%) procedure follows for all exposed patients.
Phase 8  Post-amputation inpatient stay (7–21 days — major amputation LOS
is typically longer than OLER bypass/endarterectomy).
Phase 9  Discharge disposition gate — NHD vs home discharge
Non-home (35%): 22% SNF (NUBC 03), 13% IRF/rehab (NUBC 62)
Home    (65%): NUBC 01
DEMOGRAPHIC COVARIATES — WHY NO MODULE STATES
Synthea sets age, sex, and race at patient generation (synthea.properties)
before any module runs, so demographic prevalences cannot be set from inside
a Generic Module. The Iannuzzi pipeline reads these directly:
age decades → person.year_of_birth (computed at index visit)
female      → person.gender_concept_id
nonwhite    → person.race_concept_id (NOT IN white_race concept set)
Age distribution in this module is shaped by Age_Guard + Indication_Onset_Delay
+ Age_Cap_Check; target ~30% age 60–69, ~35% age 70–79, ~25% age >=80
(major amputation cohorts skew older than OLER cohorts).
NHD OUTCOME MODELLING
Non-home discharge is a property of the index inpatient encounter, not a
post-discharge condition. The outcome is captured via discharge_disposition
on the EncounterEnd state (NUBC code written to encounters.csv DISCHARGE
column). The ETL maps NUBC codes to OMOP visit_occurrence.discharged_to_concept_id.
outcome_nhd.sql identifies outcome cohort members by discharged_to_concept_id
NOT IN the home concept set (NUBC 01/06, CMS PoS 8536, and Maps-to targets).
There is no Outcome_Onset / Outcome_Encounter / Outcome_Management state in
this module — non-home discharge is not a condition.
NHD INCIDENCE ASSUMPTIONS
Overall NHD after major LE amputation: 60–75% in real-world registries
(higher than after OLER). This module enriches to 35% NHD to keep the
validation cohort balanced. RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS in Discharge_Disposition_Branch
to match the NHD prevalence in your validation population.
Non-home destination split (of NHD cases):
SNF (NUBC 03) : 63% of NHD cases → 0.35 * 0.63 = ~22% of all patients
IRF (NUBC 62) : 37% of NHD cases → 0.35 * 0.37 = ~13% of all patients

HOW TO REVISE
1. Edit prevalence values at any Covariate_*_Check state (search RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS).
2. Edit indication mix distributions at Indication_Assignment.
3. Edit AKA/BKA mix at Index_Procedure_Branch.
4. Edit NHD rate / SNF-vs-IRF split at Discharge_Disposition_Branch.
5. Re-run: Rscript workflow/03_generate_synthea_module_artifacts.R
6. Open synthea/modules/pad_amp_nhd.diagram.html to review.
7. Re-generate CSVs: bash workflow/04_generate_synthea_csv.sh
Entry point. Transitions immediately to Age_Guard, which holds
patients below the minimum study age (60 years).
Major LE amputation is predominantly a disease of patients aged 60+.
Guard set to 60 to focus the simulation on the realistic population.
The target cohort SQL enforces min_age_at_index = 18, so younger patients
would still be valid if generated.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: change quantity to 18 to allow younger patients.
Random delay after age 60 before the qualifying indication develops.
Uniform(0, 25) years produces an onset age distribution of 60–85,
consistent with major amputation cohort age profiles.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: change high to shift the index-age distribution.
Cap to prevent simulation of implausibly aged amputation patients.
Patients over 95 at indication onset exit without procedure records.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS: change quantity to 120 to disable the cap.
INDICATION GATE — assigns each patient to one of five clinical phenotypes.
Every path issues at least one condition concept that satisfies the
PAD / DM / wound eligibility OR-clause in cohorts/target_amputation.sql.
Path distribution (RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS to match local registry mix):
35% PAD only           — chronic PAD, no documented DM/wound
25% PAD + DM           — most common dual indication in dysvascular cohorts
15% DM only            — diabetic foot complications without coded PAD
15% PAD + Wound        — CLI with ischemic ulcer/gangrene
10% Wound only         — chronic wound (e.g., diabetic foot ulcer) without coded PAD
Note: the covariate cascade (Phase 4) separately ADDS DM and tissue-loss
conditions with their own prevalences. Some path overlap is intentional —
the OMOP CDM will dedupe at the patient level when the risk score pipeline
queries for indication / mFI-5 covariate presence.
Path 1: PAD-only indication. Issues PAD ConditionOnset and routes
directly to Indication_Diagnosis_Encounter.
Path 2 step 1: PAD ConditionOnset for PAD+DM dual-indication path.
Synthea ConditionOnset states have a fixed direct_transition, so the
PAD+DM pair is modelled as a two-state sequence rather than a single
state issuing two codes.
Path 2 step 2: Diabetes mellitus ConditionOnset for PAD+DM dual-indication path.
SNOMED 73211009 → OMOP 201820 (verified 2026-04-02 in catalog).
Path 3: DM-only indication (diabetic foot complications without coded PAD).
Path 4 step 1: PAD ConditionOnset for PAD+Wound (CLI) path.
Path 4 step 2: Ischemic ulcer ConditionOnset for PAD+Wound path.

Path 5: Wound-only indication (chronic LE wound without coded PAD/DM).

Use of any walking aid documented preoperatively.
Prevalence: ~20% of OLER patients (likely higher in amputation cohorts;
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS upward if your registry shows >20%).

Verified nhd-val 2026-05-13.
value 1 = boolean presence of walking aid use.
IANNUZZI 2020 COMPONENT: Insulin-dependent diabetes — 2 points.
Operationalised as active insulin drug exposure preoperatively.
Prevalence: ~16% (raise to ~25–30% if your amputation cohort has high
diabetic representation).
Insulin glargine — RxNorm 274783 → OMOP 1502905.
Verified nhd-val 2026-05-13. Descendant of ATC 21600713 INSULINS AND
ANALOGUES (catalog insulin_dependent_diabetes_drug), which is the rollup
ancestor used in covariate_concepts.csv row insulin_dep.
IANNUZZI 2020 COMPONENT: Anemia (Hgb < 10 g/dL) — 2 points.
Hgb is measured for ALL patients (standard pre-surgical workup) so that
the missing_is_negative = FALSE flag in covariates.csv does not mark
any synthetic patient unknown. 11% receive a low value (5.5–9.9 g/dL);
89% receive a normal value (10.0–17.0 g/dL).
LOINC 718-7 Hemoglobin [vocab query — macce-val].
Haemoglobin below 10 g/dL — anaemia threshold for the Iannuzzi score.
Range 5.5–9.9 g/dL = moderate-to-severe anaemia in pre-surgical patients.
Normal haemoglobin — patient does not meet anaemia criterion.
Range 10.0–17.0 g/dL covers the normal-to-mildly-reduced spectrum.
mFI-5 COMPONENT: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease — 1 pt.
Prevalence: 15% in major-amputation cohorts (smoking-driven dysvascular
population).
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease — SNOMED 13645005 → OMOP 255573
mFI-5 COMPONENT: Congestive heart failure — 1 pt.
Subramaniam 2018 specifies CHF within 30 days prior to surgery; this
module issues CHF during the indication encounter, which is within the
pre-op window (Pre_Index_Workup_Delay = 7–90 days; some encounters fall
inside the 30-day window). For tighter timing, move CHF_Onset to a state
after Pre_Index_Workup_Delay.
Prevalence: 20% in elderly major-amputation cohorts.
Heart failure — SNOMED 84114007 → OMOP 316139 (catalog 2026-04-02).
mFI-5 COMPONENT: Hypertension — 1 pt.
Subramaniam specifies HTN requiring medication. This module does not
issue an antihypertensive MedicationOrder — the covariate set queries
the SNOMED hypertension condition (mFI-5 captures most treated HTN).
Prevalence: 65% in elderly major-amputation cohorts (very common).
Hypertensive disorder — SNOMED 38341003 → OMOP 316866 (catalog 2026-04-02).
mFI-5 COMPONENT: Dependent functional status — 1 pt.
Operationalised here as ConditionOnset of either Frailty (4086506) or
Impaired mobility (4306934) — the two ancestor concepts used in
covariate_concepts_mfi5.csv row fs_dep. The Iannuzzi ambu_deficit
covariate is intentionally separate (walking aid use observation).
Prevalence: 25% (functional dependence in elderly amputation cohorts).
Split fs_dep between the two ancestor concepts in covariate_concepts_mfi5.csv
so both branches are exercised in synthetic data. Mix: 60% Frailty, 40%
Impaired mobility.
Frailty — SNOMED 248279007 → OMOP 4086506 (catalog 2026-04-02).
Descendants include Frail elderly, Clinical frailty scale, Mild/Moderate/
Severe frailty (5 standard descendants in this vocab build).
Impaired mobility — SNOMED 82971005 → OMOP 4306934 (catalog 2026-04-02).
9 descendants including Bed-ridden, Confined to chair, Needs walking aid
in home, Mobility poor/very poor.
OVERSAMPLING DECISION POINT
Routes 10% of patients to a non-exposed pathway (no amputation, exit
without index visit) and 90% to the inpatient amputation pathway.
This aggressive oversampling enriches the validation cohort with index
events for NHD outcome modelling.
Real-world: only a fraction of patients with PAD/DM/wound progress to
major amputation. Document the institutional proportion if known.

remarks: Post-amputation inpatient stay. Major amputation LOS in major US
registries is typically 7–21 days (longer than OLER bypass / endarterectomy).
Longer LOS strongly predicts NHD via prolonged deconditioning and discharge
planning, but this module captures NHD via a fixed-probability gate rather
than LOS-conditional logic.
